hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A binary string is already sorted if all zeros precede all ones.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: If the string is already non-decreasing, zero operations are needed.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Any unsorted binary string can be sorted in a single operation by picking all out-of-order characters as the subsequence.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def minOpsToSortBinaryString(s: str) -> int:
    is_sorted = all(s[i] <= s[i + 1] for i in range(len(s) - 1))
    return 0 if is_sorted else 1
```

complexity.notes: Single pass verifies sortedness in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating sorting operations is redundant when answer is at most 1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluates condition in constant auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Observes subsequence sorting power: any binary string sorts in <= 1 op.
